Alaska's next governor asked AIDEA to wait. Its board waited. Until Tuesday.

What did Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins ask?
One hour before the meeting he asked the board to "postpone further action until after the new administration has taken office."

What did the board do?
On November 19th it met in closed session at 10 a.m. on ANWR, Ambler, real estate, assets and finances. At 3 p.m. it adjourned with no action.

What comes next?
Tuesday. The Anchorage Daily News says the board could vote then on $175 million for ANWR oil exploration. Then December 4th, three days before he takes office December 7th.

The governor-elect's request verbatim, the closed-door topics, every board date to December 7th, three AIDEA deals and two readings of his numbers.

By December 7th will the $175 million for ANWR be approved, rejected or still waiting?

#AIDEA #AlaskaPolitics #ANWR

Editor's note

Cycle 2 scores 8.67 against the round-4 threshold of 7.7, no hard fails. Art 7.5, up from 7.0 after the craft cycle, which cleared the 03 smear and completed 09; 03's door still reads ribbed rather than enamel. The Alaska Beacon citation is the feed URL because the article returned a 403. Slide 07 revisits No.113's $20 million Alaska Data Corp as context. The $200 million and $150 million are attributed readings, never summed; the $175 million is a vote the board could take.
The deck follows every honesty line in selection.md. The $200 million and $150 million are attributed to the governor-elect as the Alaska Beacon reports them, shown next to Must Read Alaska's different reading, and never added together. Nothing has him saying pause or moratorium about data centers, Tuesday has no printed date, the $175 million is only a vote the board could take, and the $75 million fiber figure is a cap. The record doesn't say when the closed session ended, so the slides say the meeting ran 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. and the session began at 10 a.m. The Beacon article page blocked fetching, so its citation is the feed URL, which will roll over.
